Subject: SOC 2 evidence and scope question - VanguardCo procurement

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for taking my call earlier. As part of our procurement and security review for Redwood’s platform, our InfoSec team has two items that need quick clarification so we can close legal:

1) Scope/exclusion: VanguardCo needs confirmation whether Redwood will be relying on a customer-managed cloud carve-out (i.e., customer is responsible for the VPC/network and certain controls) versus a subservice organization carve-out that we, as the customer, should accept. Specifically, we need a short statement describing which technical control domains are within Redwood’s SOC 2 scope and which are excluded because they reside in our customer-managed AWS account.

2) Evidence: Please provide the most recent SOC 2 Type II report for Redwood (preferred PDF), an example bridge letter that covers the audit period if Redwood relies on third-party SOC reports (e.g., AWS), and a current list of subprocessors with start/stop dates.

Target timeline: We are trying to complete legal by next Wednesday (2026-12-02). Can you confirm whether you can provide the items above by EOD Monday (2026-11-30)? If you have a standard bridge-letter template for "customer-managed cloud" scenarios, that would be ideal.

If helpful, copy me on the HubSpot record (HS-72318).

Best,
Olivia Barnes
Sr. Vendor Risk Manager
VanguardCo

Hi Olivia—thanks for the clear list. I can confirm Redwood will provide the SOC 2 Type II report and a bridge-letter covering third-party reports used during the audit period. A couple of clarifying points so we give you exactly what your InfoSec team needs: 

- When you say "customer-managed cloud carve-out," do you need a full carve-out statement that explicitly lists excluded controls (network segmentation, VPC flow logging, customer-managed key rotation), or would a shared-responsibility matrix that maps control ownership be sufficient? We can produce both, but the latter is quicker.
- For subprocessors, do you need all historical subprocessors in the audit window (past 12 months) or only currently active ones with access to customer data?

Proposed next steps: I’ll assemble the SOC 2 PDF and a draft bridge letter (we have a standard one used for AWS dependency scenarios). I’ll also include our subprocessor inventory and a brief responsibility matrix. I’m looping in Security to confirm the level of detail for the control mapping.

Can we target EOD Monday (2026-11-30)? If InfoSec needs anything sooner, let me know and I’ll prioritize.

Hi Olivia,

Thanks — we put the package together this afternoon and attached the items you requested. Summary below and attachments: 

- Redwood SOC 2 Type II (PDF): redwood_soc2_type2_2026.pdf — covers our control environment and spans 2025-01-01 to 2026-12-31 for applicable systems.
- Bridge letter: aws_bridge_letter_customer_managed_cloud.pdf — short letter that clarifies our reliance on AWS SOC 2 for infrastructure controls and the limited carve-out approach for customer-managed VPCs. The letter is scoped to the audit period and includes a statement of no shared access to customer-managed keys.
- Subprocessor inventory (CSV): subprocessor_inventory_2026.csv — list of active subprocessors during the audit window with start dates, roles, and access types.
- Responsibility matrix (inline): we included a one-page matrix summarizing ownership for Network, Logging, Key Management, and Host hardening. In short: Redwood controls application-layer auth, token management, and runtime key usage; VanguardCo (customer-managed) controls VPC configuration, customer-side KMS rotation, and inbound network ACLs when they elect a customer-managed architecture.

Notes / clarifications: 
- AWS SOC 2: we rely on AWS as a subservice organization; customers who choose a customer-managed cloud pattern will retain responsibility for VPC-level controls. Our bridge letter references the AWS SOC 2 reports (available publicly from AWS) and explains how we evaluated those reports when mapping responsibilities.
- Evidence scope: if VanguardCo requires that Redwood attest to control effectiveness in customer-managed VPCs, that would be out of scope for our SOC 2 and we can discuss compensating controls or contractual commitments (e.g., monitoring APIs, recommended baseline templates).

Next steps: I’ve uploaded the files to a shared HubSpot attachment on record HS-72318 and to the secure Drive link below.
